To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we propose the use of geolocation side information to enhance beam management in 4G and 5G NR wireless systems; and (b) we show that a machine learning approach can be used to model the relationship between the users' geolocation information and their serving beams.
we propose and evaluate a novel beam management method for 5G NR that uses geolocation information to reduce the signaling overhead and initial access latency of the beam sweeping procedure.

the proposed machine learning based beam management approach enables a 50% improvement in initial access latency, at a fixed signaling rate, or a 34% improvement in signaling rate, at a fixed latency, compared to the conventional exhaustive beam searching approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of novel machine learning methods that leverage geolocation information for the purpose of beam management in mmWave 5G NR networks.
the development of machine learning based beam management solutions for 5G NR, with the goal of reducing the initial access latency and the signaling overhead.
the design of a beam management algorithm which can be used for initial access and scheduling in a 5G NR multiuser, multi-cell mmWave deployment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our solution can be used to significantly reduce the amount of real time CSI feedback required for mmWave beam management, while maintaining the same level of network performance.
our proposed solution can enable a mmWave network to achieve a significant reduction of initial access latency and signaling overhead at a given latency requirement.
the proposed beam management methods are able to achieve the same performance as the conventional exhaustive beam search approach, while significantly reducing the signaling overhead.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an efficient machine learning based beam management solution for mmWave 5G networks which enables significant improvements in latency and signaling overhead.
the proposed beam management methods enable the network to achieve significant performance gains at a low algorithmic complexity.

we propose a novel beam management method for 5G NR that uses machine learning techniques and geolocation side information to reduce the amount and complexity of the required CSI feedback, while maintaining the network performance at a high level.
The main takeaway from our work is that

by leveraging geolocation information, we can significantly enhance the performance of 5G NR beam management algorithms, while keeping the algorithmic complexity low, and the signaling overhead reasonable.
the use of geolocation side information in conjunction with machine learning techniques, can enable significant performance gains for beam management and multiuser scheduling in 5G mmWave systems.
leveraging geolocation information can be an effective way of reducing the amount of CSI feedback required for beam management in 4G and 5G NR systems.
